text: So in (3.12) the pairing does not see $x_5$ at all (the same multipliers, the same exactness, in $M$ and in $G$), and $S\in\Delta^6$ with or without it. What $x_5$ does [computer]: it puts $128X_2^2X_1=2E_2\,X_2^2X_1$ into $\Delta^6$ (the pairing lemma alone gives $\Delta^5$), hence $B_{12}\in\Delta^6$, and it makes $B_{13}+B_{23}\in\Delta^6$ although neither term is. Dropping only its power relator $x_5^{1024}d_2^{16}$ undoes the first effect. The lift is exactly one level: at $n=7$, $128X_2^2X_1\notin\Delta^7$ in c4a (CPU, 3.8 h on a shared machine, certificate holds; c4a_lin2_n7.log). (Which identity in $\mathbb Z[G]$ does it, was not found on paper.) L2g fails at $n=7$ in $S$ (multiplier 1 where 4 is needed) and in every $B_{ij}$.

text: Call the certified level of $N\,X_{t_1}\cdots X_{t_m}$ ($N$ a power of two) the largest $\sum_r\ell_r$ over factorisations $N=\prod_rN_r$, where $\ell_r$ is the level that the pairing lemma gives to $N_rX_{t_r}$ (1 if $N_r<E_{t_r}$, else $\min(2+\log_2(N_r/E_{t_r}),k)$). It is a lower bound for the true level; relators can do better.

text: Lemma 10 [on paper]. Let $E_i\le E_j$, $A=A_{ij}=2^\alpha<E_iE_j$ (the pair of Lemma 9). The certified level of $\binom A2X_j^2X_i$ is at most $k+2=c+1$. Proof. $v_2\binom A2=\alpha-1\le a_i+a_j-2$. Raising $X_j$ to level $\ge2$ costs $\ge a_j$, and then $\le a_i-2<a_i$ is left: the other two factors stay at level 1, total $\le k+2$. Otherwise only $X_i$ is raised, to $\le k$: total $\le k+2$. $\square$

text: The bilinear model of §6.9 with free coefficients $p_{il}$ does have multiplier-4 solutions. [on paper] With only $d_2$ in the relators ($x_1^{E_1}=d_2^{p_{12}}$, $x_3^{E_3}=d_2^{p_{32}}$) the conditions reduce to $v_2(q_{21}p_{12})=v_2(q_{23}p_{32})<a_2$ and two inequalities that hold for $A_{13}$ large; with $E_1=E_2=E_3$ the multiplier does not enter at all (the $d_l$ have order $\le E_l$, so $\gcd(4E_i,E_l)=E_l$). [computer, scripts/c5_split_screen.py] For equal orders $E\le2^6$, $p_{il}\in\{0,\pm1,\pm2\}$: 40 solutions, the cheapest $E=4$, $A=(4,8,4)$, $p_{12}=\pm2$, $p_{32}=\pm2$. But the model's "$w\ne0$" is not reliable: of four such groups built in GAP (eq4a, eq4b, eq8a, eq8b: $E=4$ or $8$ for all three, $P_1=d_2^{\pm2}$, $P_3=d_2^{2}$, class 5, $t=[x_4,x_3,x_3]$) three have $w=1$ in $M$, and in eq8a ($w$ of order 2) all $g_i=1$ exactly — $S=0$, $w$ is pure binomial error, and $w\in D_5\setminus D_6$ (certified) [computer].
